## MM-20210812 — WhatsApp (founders Brian Acton and Jan Koum) and its owner Facebook
hook (question, until 24s): If you're not paying for the product you are the product; how does WhatsApp make money? A simple question that led to a much darker rabbit hole.
thesis: What started out as a very simple business question led me down a rabbit hole much darker than I would have imagined that affects every single one of us.
beats: setup → setup → rise → rise → turn → explainer → fall → obstacle → explainer → aftermath → sponsor → climax → outro
twist: Facebook buys unprofitable WhatsApp for $19 billion, turning an anti-ads, pro-privacy app into part of the data business it opposed.
open loops: How does WhatsApp make money? | Why would Facebook pay $19 billion for an unprofitable app? | Zuckerberg promised independence and no pressure to monetise: what could go wrong?
ending: callback: Repeats the opening line, 'if you're not paying for the product, you are the product', after a balanced take on whether to leave WhatsApp; then next-episode outro.

## MM-20211213 — Travis Kalanick and Uber
hook (irony, until 41.6s): Uber is called the most ethically challenged company in Silicon Valley; its idea was revolutionary but illegal.
thesis: The story of Uber is littered with scandals and controversy at every single turn.
beats: setup → setup → rise → obstacle → rise → obstacle → sponsor → fall → fall → fall → climax → aftermath → outro
twist: Travis, on leave to 'work on himself', is forced out as CEO by board and investors.
open loops: Not a typical business story: the idea was illegal | An even bigger battle was just beginning (Lyft) | Things are about to get even more controversial
ending: open_question: Callback to the Paris night and 'end of the ride'; then asks if Uber without Travis is like Apple without Jobs; then subscribe outro.
